avenues.name: The achievement ledger
avenues.thesis: A 270-row, event-anchored, per-row-verified corpus of US and Chinese achievements 1926–2026; 268 rows ESTABLISHED under a published promotion standard, with the full 1926–2025 chronological corpus now processed.

avenues.name: Coverage shape
avenues.thesis: Facts about the corpus under the published selection rule: US coverage is steady and invention/deployment-heavy; China's is thin early, rises late, and is completion/milestone-heavy. A statement about the ledger — NOT a momentum verdict about the world.

avenues.name: The momentum index
avenues.thesis: Now computed and shown as a constructed index (Option C gate: ESTABLISHED rows only, non-ESTABLISHED rows excluded and named). Primary = baseline equal weighting; bands span four published weightings; whiskers show the 1946–1955 exclusion. Re-weightable, rubric published — true only within its scope, never a measured verdict.

avenues.name: Early-century China floor
avenues.thesis: 1926–1945 China coverage is a floor, not a fact — real historical thinness compounded by English-language source bias. Posted as an open challenge: readers who know this literature can raise it, for named credit.

avenues.name: Verification in progress
avenues.thesis: Live status: 268 ESTABLISHED, 1 OPEN-UNVERIFIED, 1 REPORTED. Batches 1–10 processed the full 1926–2025 corpus; a straggler sweep then removed one un-anchorable row and converted two more into anchored, verified rows. Just ONE row stays open: the Chengdu–Chongqing Railway (CN-1952-1) — its July 1952 opening is uncontested, but no independent non-PRC source has been found, so it is posted as an open challenge (named credit for whoever closes it). The 2026 window is also not yet closed.

checks._comment: Single source of truth for the consistency-check RULES. Both index.html's console and verification/verify_numbers.py read these, so a threshold can never drift between the page and the verifier. Change a rule HERE and both sides enforce it on next run. (The check LOGIC is still written in each language — see AUTHORING.md — but the rules it enforces live only here.)
